title: Book Two · Chapter 164: A Game with Jun
story:
Jun is alone in the yard with a cloth ball. He throws it against the wall and catches it twice. On the third throw, it strikes a loose patch and jumps sideways.

Ronan catches it near the path.

“The wall is on my side,” he says.

“The wall has no idea.”

Jun holds out his hands. Ronan throws the ball back. It lands low, and Jun has to bend quickly.

“You can join,” Jun says. “Keep it away from the windows.”

Ronan takes his place. They make a simple game: five catches each, then a change of places. The ball bounces sideways once for Ronan and twice for Jun. Jun says that is unfair. Ronan offers to trade places with the wall.

They play until both are warm. Then they sit on the low edge beside the steps. Ronan has a water bottle. He offers it. Jun has his own.

For a little while, they watch younger children cross the yard. Ronan's last practice is tomorrow. Jun's drawing work is already on a classroom board.

“Your round horse is still there,” Ronan says.

“Cow.”

“I am keeping both choices open.”

Jun smiles. He picks a loose thread from the ball and presses it under the cloth.

Ronan wants to ask about working together again. He asks before he can stop himself.

“If I get into the group, could you help with a new route page?”

Jun looks at the ball.

“I have other work.”

“Only one page.”

“Ronan.”

He stops. Jun's voice is quiet, but the answer is clear.

“All right,” Ronan says. “I heard you.”

Jun takes a drink. Ronan looks at his shoes. They were having fun before his question. He wants to find an easier topic, but he says nothing.

A younger child runs past with one shoe lace loose. Ronan watches until the child reaches the far steps.

He turns back. Jun is looking at the ball, not at him.

Ronan starts to explain that a route page would be small. He stops before the words come out. Jun already heard that part.

The ball has a pale patch near one seam. Ronan points to it.

“Is that where it hits the wall?”

“Mostly. I keep trying to turn it.”

“Does it turn back?”

“Every time.”

Jun rolls the ball between his palms. The pale patch comes into view again.

Ronan smiles. He takes a drink and puts the bottle beside his bag. He does not move closer to Jun or ask about the drawing work.

Jun gives the ball one small toss and catches it himself. Then he looks up at Ronan.

“Do you want another game?” Jun asks at last.

“Yes.”

They stand. This time, Ronan throws too hard. The ball passes Jun and rolls under the bench. Ronan goes to get it himself.

When he returns, he asks about Jun's next drawing. Jun says it is a street with no animals. Ronan says the wall can be in it if it behaves.

Jun laughs, and the game starts again. They finish five catches each. Neither boy says anything about a route page.

At the gate, they go in different directions. Jun lifts the ball once in goodbye. Ronan lifts his hand and walks toward River Street. They still had fun this afternoon. Jun said no to the new page. Ronan will not ask again today.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

bounce＝弹跳；trade places＝交换位置；thread＝线头；behave＝表现规矩。

## 理解问题

1. Jun愿意和Ronan做什么，又拒绝了什么？
2. Ronan接受拒绝后，两人的下午怎样继续？

## 读句子

**He offers it.**

拆开看：He / offers / it.

他／递出／它。
